relevance_note: Family case report of seven labelled relatives carrying a TNFAIP3 variant: 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20' after a 'heterozygous c.2209delC mutation' was found.
method_note: Written by hand from the text with a small Python builder; no table transcription. Tables 1 and 2 (thyroid tests, HLA typing) and Figs. 1-2 are captions only in the Markdown, so their contents (e.g. P2-P4 antibody levels, the pedigree) are not available and nothing was taken from them. Variant, zygosity, transcript and diagnosis come from the named-group statements 'analyzed TNFAIP3 in the present family (P1–P7) ... heterozygous c.2209delC mutation that was present in all members tested' and 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20'; transcript NM_006290.2 is printed for this variant. Functional evidence and pathogenicity come from the sentence about 'this variant' (previous in vitro analysis, ref 2); the paper also calls it 'novel'. Variant type not stated, so not reported. Inheritance: only P1 recorded as inherited maternal (P2 is named as P1's mother and carries the variant). P2 (mother P3 by implication of 'maternal grandmother'), P4 (maternal uncle), P7 (younger sister) and the cousins P5/P6 were left not reported because the paper does not state their parent-child links explicitly. Hashimoto's thyroiditis diagnosis ages (P2 28 yr, P3 27 yr) are recorded in phenotypic feature details, not in age_at_diagnosis (which was taken to mean the HA20 diagnosis; not reported). P1, P6, P7 'have normal thyroid functions and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies, but are too young for this to be apparent': recorded as excluded abnormal thyroid function / anti-thyroid autoantibodies and checklist autoimmune thyroiditis excluded; the broader checklist 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' left not reported. Stomatitis (P3, P4) was not mapped to checklist 'oral ulcers'; possible Crohn's disease (P2) and perineal fistula 'possibly associated with inflammatory bowel disease' (P7) and P1's bloody stools were not mapped to the GI inflammation checklist item; P4's Hodgkin lymphoma and craniopharyngioma were not mapped to lymphoproliferation or CNS involvement checklist items (kept as feature rows). P2's cervical lymphadenitis was mapped to lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy. Ethnicity 'Japanese' from the statement that this family was part of a study of 'HA20 patients in nine independent Japanese families (2)'. n_patients_reported=7 counts the enumerated P1–P7. Sex of P1 and P6 not stated. No internal contradictions found.
